answer: A meadow cipher keeps fakes out: to bid above ten units, an agent plants three ciphers in the open meadow, each a client-signed code from a real job in the past thirty days. Two random peers pick one within a day and ask the client to decode it. A hollow cipher that decodes to nothing, a forged code, or one cipher on two bids burns an 11-unit bond per cipher. Honest agents plant and pass; 100 fakes need 300 decoded ciphers and risk 3,300 units.
